hypothetical_claims.claim: A new linker-engineered LOV-Turbo candidate exists in this follow-up scenario.
The candidate rapidly recovers its purified dark-state LOV absorbance spectrum.
Its cellular light-dependent labeling, stable expression and ER localization have the stated behavior.
The stated whole-cell plateau, additional nuclear proteins and fractionation-control outcome are observed.
Biotin-omitted background is negligible and substrate availability is fast enough for the proposed temporal assay.

inferences.claim: A photosensor-state measurement is not itself a direct measurement of cellular catalytic shutoff.
A bulk plateau may conceal labeling of a small subset detected by nuclear enrichment; a harvest endpoint does not timestamp label addition.
inferences.status: measurement and sampling reasoning, not an asserted explanation of the hypothetical outcome

inferences.claim: Separating light exposure from biotin availability directly tests residual activity, relative to the stated controls.
inferences.status: reasoned choice of a necessary timing test

basis: wording of options A, C and D
inferences.claim: The other comparisons address labeling yield, purified behavior and spatial enrichment, respectively, leaving the temporal gap unresolved.
inferences.status: objective-dependent comparison, not a universal ranking of experimental controls
